'''Harrison Bryce Jordan Barnes'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/kevin_armstrong/06/26/harrison.barnes/index.html |title=Ames High guard Harrison Barnes is nation's top hoops recruit - Kevin Armstrong - SI.com |publisher=Sportsillustrated.cnn.com |date=2009-06-29 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> (born May 30, 1992) is an [[United States|American]] college [[basketball]] player. He is a sophomore at [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and was one of the top rated basketball players in the recruiting class of 2010.<!-- Before tagging this for citation, see the scout.com reference below -->  Barnes is sometimes known by the nickname "Black Falcon."<ref>[http://blogs.newsobserver.com/accnow/barnes-black-falcoln-nickname-came-from-espn Barnes' 'Black Falcon' nickname came from ESPN], accessed March 22, 2011</ref>

==High school career==
[[File:Harrison Barnes.jpg|thumb|left|Barnes (right) with [[Kyrie Irving]] while playing for the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]].]]
Harrison Barnes was rated as the number 1 player in the class of 2010 by [[Scout.com]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2010 |title=Scout.com: Football Recruiting |publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> and in the [[ESPNU]] 100.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2010&action=upsell&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100%3f%26season%3d2010 |title=College Basketball Recruiting - ESPNU 100 - ESPN |publisher=Insider.espn.go.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> He was rated as the number 2 player by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1909 |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking - Rivals150 for class of 2010 |publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> In his junior year, Barnes led [[Ames High School]] to an Iowa 4A state championship where he had 24 points and 8 rebounds, capping off a 26-0 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dailycontributor.com/top-rated-basketball-recruit-harrison-barnes-chooses-north-carolina/8627/ |title=Top-Rated Basketball Recruit Harrison Barnes Chooses North Carolina |publisher=Daily Contributor |date=2009-11-13 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> In his senior year, Barnes led Ames to a 27-0 season and a second straight Iowa 4A state championship becoming Iowa's big-school class's first team to go undefeated in consecutive seasons. In the finals he scored 19 points against [[Southeast Polk]]. He averaged 26.1 points, 10.0 rebounds, 3.1 steals and 3.0 assists during his senior year and was selected to the ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA First Team.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Halley|first=Jim|url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2010-all-usa-boys.htm|title=2010 All-USA boys basketball: Harrison Barnes leads the way|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 21, 2010 |accessdate=September 11, 2011}}</ref> Barnes capped off his Ames High School career as their all-time leading scorer with 1,787 points.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.timesrepublican.com/page/content.detail/id/523886.html?nav=5010 |title=Carolina-bound Barnes named Mr. Basketball - TimesRepublican.com | News, Sports, Jobs, Community info |publisher=Times Republican |date=2010-03-16 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> Barnes played in the 4th annual [[Boost Mobile]] Elite 24 Hoops Classic where he scored 18 points for Skip To My Lou.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Name |first=Author |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/college/2009/08/elite-24-recap-2/ |title=Elite 24 Recap |publisher=Slam Online |date=2009-08-22 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref>
On January 20, 2010, it was announced that Barnes was selected to the 2010 Junior National Select Team. The team played at the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Rose Garden (arena)|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon]] on April 10.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Name |first=Author |url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/01/its-the-usa-against-everyone-else/ |title=It’s the USA Against Everyone Else |publisher=Slam Online |date=2010-01-20 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> He was also selected to play in the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American Game]] where he led the West team to a 107-104 victory. He scored a team high 18 points and was named co-MVP with [[Jared Sullinger]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/m2xSkj0QEd-lugAcxJTdpg/mcdonalds-all-american-night--knights-3-pointer-wins-it-for-the-west.htm |title=McDonald's All-American night: Knight's 3-pointer wins it for the West - MaxPreps News |publisher=Maxpreps.com |date=2010-03-31 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> He also played in the 2010 Jordan Brand Classic where he was named co-MVP with Kyrie Irving.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nike.com/jumpman23/classic/2010jbc.html |title=Jordan Brand Classic |publisher=Nike.com |date=2010-02-18 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> On March 10, 2010, Barnes won the Morgan Wootten Player of the Year Award, which goes to the nation's top player.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Halley |first=Jim |url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2010-03-10-morgan-wootten-player-of-the-year_N.htm |title=Iowa's Harrison Barnes named Morgan Wootten Player of the Year |publisher=Usatoday.Com |date=2010-03-10 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref>

===AAU===
Barnes played for the "Howard Pulley Panthers" on the [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] circuit alongside current [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]] [[offensive lineman]] [[Seantrel Henderson]], who was one of the nation's top football prospects in the class of 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4647030 |title=Harrison Barnes and Seantrel Henderson formed a one-two punch on the Twin Cities-based Pulley Panthers AAU team. - ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=2009-11-12 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref>

===SLAM Magazine===
Barnes was the 2010 high school diary keeper for [[SLAM Magazine]].

Barnes considered offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4651146 |title=North Carolina Tar Heels paid SF Harrison Barnes, the No. 11 player in the 2010 class. - ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=2009-11-13 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref><ref name="scout1">{{Cite web|url=http://northcarolina.scout.com/2/919368.html |title=Scout.com: Barnes to UNC |publisher=Northcarolina.scout.com |date=2009-11-13 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> Barnes unofficially visited Kansas twice, for [[Midnight Madness (basketball)|Late Night in the Phog]] in October 2008 and a spring game against Tennessee.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Temple |first=Jesse |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2009/may/04/pump-n-run-n-done/ |title=Pump N Run ‘n’ done |publisher=KUsports.com |date=2009-05-04 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> Barnes took official visits to North Carolina, Duke, Kansas, UCLA, and Oklahoma, but he did not take an official visit to Iowa State; since he only lives a mile from campus, he chose to unofficially visit instead.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.reflector.com/news/state/iowas-harrison-barnes-cuts-college-list-to-6-793523.html |title=The Daily Reflector |publisher=Reflector.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref>  On November 13, 2009, Barnes [[Skype]]d coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] of the North Carolina Tar Heels, making UNC his future [[alma mater]].<ref name="scout1"/>

==College career==
Barnes had 21 points in his North Carolina debut in an exhibition game in the [[Bahamas]] against the Commonwealth Bank Giants. UNC won the game 130-87.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://acc.blogs.starnewsonline.com/14866/impressive-debut-for-barnes-in-the-bahamas/ |title=Impressive debut for Barnes in the Bahamas – ACC Insider - Wilmington Star News - Wilmington, NC - Archive |publisher=Acc.blogs.starnewsonline.com |date=2010-08-11 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> Overall, Barnes averaged 22 points and 6.5 rebounds per game for UNC in the Bahamas.<ref>{{Cite web|author=Perry Missner |url=http://www.collegefantasyhoopsinsider.com/news/15624/Harrison-Barnes-shines-in-Bahamas |title=Harrison Barnes shines in Bahamas |publisher=College Fantasy Hoops Insider |date=2010-08-14 |accessdate=2010-08-24}}</ref> On November 1, 2010, Barnes was named a preseason All-American by the AP.  He is the first [[freshman]] to ever receive this honor.<ref>{{Cite web|author=Jim O'Connell |url=http://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20101101/ap_on_sp_co_ne/bkc_preseason_all_america |title=Singler, Pullen top AP preseason All-America team |publisher=Yahoo! News |date=2010-11-01 |accessdate=2010-11-03}}</ref> Barnes had 14 points and 4 rebounds in his North Carolina debut vs. Lipscomb.<ref>{{Cite web|author= |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=303160153&campaign=rss&source=ESPNHeadlines |title=Super freshman Harrison Barnes scores 14 as UNC rolls in opener |publisher=ESPN News |date=November 12, 2010 |accessdate=November 12, 2010}}</ref> He recorded his first career double double on December 11, 2010, scoring 19 points and snatching 10 rebounds in a 96-91 victory over Long Beach State University.<ref>{{Cite web|author= |url=http://carolinaupdate.com/north-carolina-basketball/game-recap/north-carolina-looks-good-in-close-96-91-win-over-long-beach-state |title=Harrison Barnes Records First Career Double Double |publisher=CarolinaUpdate.com |date=December 12, 2010 |accessdate=January 3, 2011}}</ref>  

Barnes' previous career high of 26 points came against Boston College on February 1, 2011.  He surpassed this mark on March 12, 2011 in an ACC tournament game against Clemson, scoring 40 points while also grabbing 8 rebounds. Additionally, Barnes's 40 point performance set the record for points by a Freshman in an ACC Tournament game.<ref>{{Cite web|author= |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310710153|title=Tar Heels seal spot in ACC final as Harrison Barnes scores season-high 40 |publisher=ESPN News |date=March 12, 2011 |accessdate=March 12, 2011}}</ref> On April 18, 2011, Barnes announced that he would return to North Carolina for his sophomore season. 

Barnes is the ninth UNC Tar Heel to earn ACC Rookie of Year recognition, and the fourth to do so under Coach Roy Williams.  During his freshman year at UNC, he became the 14th Tar Heel to earn Freshman All-American honors and also became the 11th freshman to earn first-team All-ACC Tournament honors.  Barnes scored the most points, as a freshman, in the ACC tournament since Phil Ford scored 78 points in 1975.  He then went on to the NCAA tournament where he scored 84 points, the most points of any UNC freshman in history.
